newsitem.title: CHINA: Cambodia's Ranariddh in China for private visit.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh in China for private visit.

text.p: Cambodia's ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh arrived in China on Friday for what officials insist is a private visit to his father King Norodom Sihanouk.
Chinese officials whisked Ranariddh out of the airport amid tight security and he did not speak to reporters.
China has said Ranariddh, deposed this month in a coup by his rival Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, is in China only to visit his father and will not engage in any political activities.
Sihanouk issued a statement saying the visit was purely private.
The king, who reigns but does not rule in Cambodia, maintains a residence in Beijing, where he has been undergoing medical treatment for several months.

"My son...wishes simply to see me after a separation of several months," said Sihanouk on Thursday. He said that, as a constitutional monarch, he took no sides in the dispute between the two prime ministers.

Ranariddh, who has crossed three continents in the past two weeks to press his cause with government and U.N. leaders, made a brief visit to Thailand on Thursday to meet special U.S. envoy on Cambodia Stephen Solarz to discuss how best to solve the problem in his homeland.
Solarz was in Cambodia on Friday to meet Cambodian strongman Hun Sen.
Earlier in the week, Ranariddh visited Singapore and Jakarta.
Ranariddh has vowed to travel the world to drum up international support for a non-violent solution to the crisis in Cambodia in an effort to prevent civil war.
Aides have said Ranariddh planned also to go to Japan and then return to Europe. Ranariddh was in France during the bloody takeover in Phnom Penh.
